title: Slice 7: Role-based theme MVP (types + downgrade + 2 built-ins)
description:
MVP of the theme engine per docs/specs/theming.md. Delivers visible colored output end-to-end with 2 built-in themes.

Scope:
- Role enum (16 variants: 9 base + 7 extended per spec)
- Color enum (TrueColor / Palette256 / Palette16 / NoColor)
- Style struct (minimal: role + fg override + bold/italic/underline/dim). Skip hyperlink + bg for MVP.
- Theme struct: Role → Color map + name + extended-role fallback table
- Terminal capability detection via `supports-color` crate
- Downgrade resolver: truecolor → 256 → 16 → none
- Segment API so segments opt into a role (e.g. `RenderedSegment::with_role(Role::Primary)` or a Style on SegmentDefaults)
- Wire through render path: layout emits ANSI around segment text per resolved theme
- 2 built-in themes compiled in:
  - `default`: neutral, uses Palette16 so it works on every terminal
  - `minimal`: no colors, decorations only (bold/dim/italic)
- Config resolution: `theme = "default"` / `theme = "minimal"` looked up in the built-in registry; unknown name falls back to `default` with a stderr warning

Deliberately OUT of scope (follow-ups):
- Catppuccin 4 flavors (new bead, blocked on this)
- User theme TOML loading + discovery (new bead, blocked on this)
- Style-string syntax parser ("role:success bold") (new bead, blocked on this)
- `linesmith themes list` subcommand (new bead, blocked on this)
- User per-segment style overrides from config.toml (new bead, blocked on this)
- NO_COLOR / FORCE_COLOR env vars + --no-color / --force-color flags (already lsm-xhx)

Tests: role → color mapping, downgrade table, segment emits expected ANSI, capability detection honored, unknown-theme fallback, extended-role fallback.
close_reason: MVP theme engine shipped: Role enum (9 base + 7 extended), Color (TrueColor/Palette256/Palette16/NoColor), Style, Theme, Capability with supports-color detection + NO_COLOR honored, truecolor→256→16 downgrade, RenderContext threaded through render path, SGR emission per-segment via layout::render_with_warn, 2 built-ins (default + minimal), 6 built-in segments declare roles. 240 lib + 7 integration tests. title: RFC: Extract CLI driver + segment builder from lib.rs
description:
## Problem

lib.rs is ~1300 lines and co-hosts five concerns: the render façade (`run`, `run_with_width`, `run_with_segments_and_width`, `run_with_context`, `RenderContext`), width detection, segment assembly with override validation, the CLI driver (`CliEnv`, `cli_main`, `run_cli`, `load_config`, `check_config`, `resolve_theme`), and ~740 lines of tests across two inline modules. Navigating any single concern requires understanding the whole file; adding tests to one domain requires reading the others. The render façade legitimately belongs at the crate root, but the CLI orchestration and segment assembly are implementation details that leak into the public-API file.

## Proposed Interface

Two new modules, each with a minimal surface. All existing `linesmith::*` paths preserved via re-exports; `main.rs` and `tests/integration.rs` do not change.

### `crate::driver` (new file `src/driver.rs`)

Public surface — two items:

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct CliEnv {
    pub linesmith_config: Option<String>,
    pub xdg_config_home: Option<String>,
    pub home: Option<String>,
    pub terminal_width: Option<u16>,
    pub color_capability: Option<crate::theme::Capability>,
}

impl CliEnv {
    pub fn from_process() -> Self;  // snapshot real env
    pub fn for_tests() -> Self;     // None paths, width=Some(200), capability=Some(None)
    pub fn empty() -> Self;         // all None — for tests asserting on lazy detection
}

pub fn cli_main<A>(
    args: A,
    stdin: impl std::io::Read,
    stdout: &mut dyn std::io::Write,
    stderr: &mut dyn std::io::Write,
    env: &CliEnv,
) -> u8
where A: IntoIterator, A::Item: Into<std::ffi::OsString>;
```

Crate-private: `run_cli`, `load_config`, `check_config`, `resolve_theme` become `fn` (no `pub`).

### `crate::segments::builder` (new file `src/segments/builder.rs`)

Public surface — two items:

```rust
pub fn build(config: Option<&crate::config::Config>, warn: impl FnMut(&str)) -> Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>;
pub fn build_default() -> Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>;
```

Crate-private: `apply_override`.

### Crate-root re-exports (in `lib.rs`)

```rust
pub use driver::{cli_main, CliEnv};
pub use segments::builder::{build as build_segments, build_default as build_default_segments};
```

Rename-on-re-export preserves integration-test call sites.

## Dependency Strategy

**In-process** — all logic is pure plus thin I/O wrappers. Nothing crosses a network/process boundary. No new traits or adapters introduced; external-crate wrappers (`supports-color`, `terminal-size`, `toml`, `serde_json`) already live as single-function seams that can be swapped in place.

## Testing Strategy

**Test relocation** — replace, don't layer:

- `cli_main_tests` module (15 tests, ~540 lines) moves from `lib.rs` → `driver.rs`
- `build_segments_*` tests (~8 tests, plus `StubWithWidth` + `width_merge_*` = 12 tests total, ~200 lines) move from `lib.rs::tests` → `segments/builder.rs::tests`
- Width detection tests + `resolve_terminal_width` tests stay in `lib.rs`
- Render-path tests (`malformed_json_renders_marker_and_succeeds`, `minimal_payload_renders_model_then_workspace`, `full_payload_renders_model_context_workspace`) stay in `lib.rs`
- Integration tests at `tests/integration.rs` untouched

**No new tests added** — this is a move refactor. Test count stays at 240 lib + 7 integration.

**New `CliEnv::for_tests()` constructor** replaces the duplicated `fn empty_env()` helper inside `cli_main_tests`. Net LOC reduction ~10 lines of test setup.

## Implementation Recommendations

### What `driver` owns

- Args → exit code (the full CLI lifecycle)
- Config path resolution, load, validation
- `--check-config` exit-code contract (0 ok / 1 invalid)
- Lazy width + capability detection on render path only
- Theme name resolution with unknown-name warning + fallback
- IO wiring through injected stdin/stdout/stderr sinks

### What `driver` hides

- That arg parsing goes through `lexopt` via `cli::parse`
- That config loading is a two-step resolve-then-read
- That `--check-config` has four failure modes (no-path / invalid-parse / no-file-implicit / valid-with-warnings)
- The specific env vars (`LINESMITH_CONFIG`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `HOME`) and their precedence

### What `driver` exposes

- `CliEnv` as the sole input struct for ambient process state
- `cli_main` as the sole orchestration entry point
- `u8` exit code (callers wrap in `ExitCode` at the binary boundary)

### What `segments::builder` owns

- `Config` → `Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>` transformation
- Validation: unknown IDs warn + skip, duplicates keep-first, empty-list warning, inverted-bounds drop with warning
- Override application: priority + width-with-inherit-from-inner-default

### What `segments::builder` hides

- The `DEFAULT_SEGMENT_IDS` canonical order
- The `OverriddenSegment` wrapper (applied internally when a `[segments.<id>]` table exists)
- Width-bounds merge algorithm (caller supplies half-specified bounds; builder inherits the other half from the segment's built-in default)

### What `segments::builder` exposes

- Two free functions keyed on `Option<&Config>` + warn callback
- Return type `Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>` unchanged from today

### Migration

- `main.rs` and `tests/integration.rs` keep working unchanged — re-exports handle the path shift
- `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `lib.rs` loses its width + build_segments blocks but keeps render tests
- No public API deletions; no breaking changes

## Scope boundary

Explicitly NOT in this refactor:
- Extension traits for plugin runtime (`lsm-ewa` owns that design)
- Theme registry trait for user-loaded themes (`lsm-qp5` owns that)
- External-crate leak tightening (separate bead — tighten `lexopt::Error` / `toml::de::Error` surfaces out of public API)
- `cli_main_from_process()` convenience wrapper (net-zero move, adds surface for no gain)
- `theme::catppuccin` sketch (belongs in `lsm-b7u`)

## Expected impact

- `lib.rs`: ~1300 → ~400 lines (render façade + width + re-exports + render tests)
- `driver.rs`: new, ~250 lines + ~540 test lines
- `segments/builder.rs`: new, ~90 lines + ~210 test lines
- Public API: zero surface change
- Test count: unchanged (240 lib + 7 integration)
- Follow-ups enabled: any future module deepening can happen inside `driver` or `builder` without touching `lib.rs`
close_reason: Extracted CLI driver into crate::driver and segment assembly into crate::segments::builder. lib.rs: 1206 → 273 lines (77% reduction). Both new modules pub(crate) so re-exports at crate root (linesmith::cli_main, linesmith::CliEnv, linesmith::build_segments, linesmith::build_default_segments) are the canonical paths. Added CliEnv::for_tests() named constructor replacing the anonymous empty_env() helper. Test count unchanged (240 lib + 7 integration). No public API change. Codex review + 5-agent review pass confirmed byte-identical behavior.

title: Slice 7c: User theme loading + style syntax + themes subcommand
description:
Follow-up to lsm-7kn (MVP theme engine). Lets users ship their own themes and override per-segment styling.

Scope:
- Theme TOML file format parser (per docs/specs/theming.md §Theme file format)
- User theme discovery: `~/.config/linesmith/themes/*.toml` at startup, XDG-compliant
- Name-collision handling: user theme wins over built-in of same name, stderr warning
- Parse error handling: reject invalid theme with diagnostic, don't crash; fall back to `default`
- Style string syntax parser: `"role:success bold"`, `"fg:#ff8800 underline"`, `"fg:red dim"`
- User per-segment style overrides via config.toml: `[segments.<id>] style = "..."`
- Resolution precedence wiring: user override → segment style → theme role → downgrade (env vars are lsm-xhx scope)
- `linesmith themes list` CLI subcommand: enumerate built-ins + user themes, with source annotation

Acceptance: drop a theme.toml in ~/.config/linesmith/themes/, reference it via `theme = "<name>"`, see it render. User per-segment style overrides work. `themes list` shows both built-in and user themes.

title: Slice 7b: Catppuccin flavors (Latte/Frappé/Macchiato/Mocha)
description:
Follow-up to lsm-7kn (MVP theme engine). Ships the 4 Catppuccin flavors against the MVP theme registry so linesmith qualifies for the Catppuccin integration list (github.com/catppuccin/catppuccin#portlist).

Scope:
- Depend on `catppuccin` crate (~20KB) OR embed 4 TOML palettes via include_str!. Decision point during implementation; crate is leaner for palette drift detection.
- Register 4 flavors in the built-in theme registry: catppuccin-latte, catppuccin-frappe, catppuccin-macchiato, catppuccin-mocha
- Map all 9 base roles to Catppuccin palette colors per flavor
- Map all 7 extended roles to flavor-appropriate dim/surface/border variants
- Snapshot tests: render a canonical status-line through each flavor, assert expected bytes
- Palette-sync CI check: detect upstream Catppuccin palette changes

Acceptance: `theme = "catppuccin-mocha"` in config.toml renders with the Mocha palette; 4 flavors all recognized; snapshot tests lock the output per flavor.

title: Make main.rs run() and check_config() testable via pure inner fn
description:
From slice-8 (lsm-u8u) review: main.rs has ~100 lines of orchestration (arg error paths, load/fallback logic, --check-config branches) with zero direct tests. Integration tests hit linesmith::run_* which bypasses main entirely.

Extract pure inner function: fn run_inner(args, stdin, stdout, stderr, env) -> ExitCode. Then main.rs becomes a thin wrapper that reads env + delegates. Tests spawn the inner function with fake IO and assert exit codes + byte output.

Alternative: use assert_cmd / std::process::Command to spawn the built binary against fixture configs. Simpler but slower and less portable.

Closing the gap matters because --check-config's exit codes (0 for ok, 1 for invalid) are the CI/editor-integration contract per docs/specs/config.md:245. Today a regression that flips those codes ships green.
notes: Expanded scope post-Codex review: also threaded stderr through run_with_segments_and_width + layout::render (superseded lsm-v3e), and changed terminal_width to Option<u16> so meta commands don't probe TTY.
close_reason: Extracted cli_main(args, stdin, stdout, stderr, env) -> u8 into lib.rs; main.rs shrinks to a 10-line ExitCode wrapper. 12 new tests lock --check-config exit codes (0 ok / 1 no-path / 1 malformed / 0 missing-explicit), help/version output, bad-arg hint, and CliEnv plumbing (HOME/XDG precedence). Follow-up filed for run_with_segments_and_width stderr plumbing.

title: Warn on unknown keys in config.toml (not just silently ignore)
description:
From slice-8 (lsm-u8u) review: spec (docs/specs/config.md §Validation rules §1/§6) says unknown top-level keys should WARN and be ignored, and unknown keys in [segments.<id>] blocks should WARN and be ignored. The current impl silently ignores all unknown keys (no #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] anywhere) because deny_unknown_fields rejected spec-valid forward-compat keys like 'theme', '$schema', 'layout'.

Correct fix requires a two-phase parse: first parse into a tolerant struct for backwards/forwards compat, then validate the raw toml::Value tree against a known-key allow-list and emit warnings. That's more work than this slice needed.

User impact today: typos like 'priorty = 10' silently drop instead of warning. Matters more once --check-config becomes a CI gate.
close_reason: Unknown-key warnings via two-phase parse (toml::Value → validate_keys → try_into). Allow-lists: top-level (implemented + spec-documented forward-compat), [layout_options] fields, per-segment schema that tightly gates built-ins while skipping unknown ids so plugins own their own schema. Warnings surface on render stderr and count toward --check-config summary. 17 new tests (281 lib + 7 integration).

title: Multi-line layout: [line.N] sections + layout="multi-line"
description:
Support multi-line status lines per docs/specs/config.md §Multi-line layouts.

Config shape:
- layout = "multi-line" at top level
- [line.1] segments = [...]
- [line.2] segments = [...]
Each line runs the layout algorithm independently, emits its own newline-terminated string.

Edge cases (from spec edge-case table):
- layout = "multi-line" with no [line.N] sections → treat as single-line, warn
- layout = "single-line" with [line.N] sections present → info log, use [line] for rendering
- [line] AND [line.N] both present → document precedence

Depends on lsm-u8u (config parser) and lsm-aql (layout engine — already shipped).

title: Color policy: --no-color / --force-color + NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR + [layout_options]
description:
Wire color emission through CLI flags, env vars, and config.

**Precedence (first match wins):**
1. `--no-color` or `--force-color` CLI flag
2. `NO_COLOR` env var (per no-color.org, any non-empty value)
3. `FORCE_COLOR` env var (any non-empty value)
4. `[layout_options].color = "auto"|"always"|"never"` in config
5. Default "auto" (TTY detection via supports-color)

**Also in this slice:**
- `[layout_options].claude_padding` — factored into width calc before handing to layout

**Out of scope (filed as follow-up):**
- `[layout_options].separator` styles (`powerline`, `capsule`, `flex`). Powerline needs Nerd Font glyph emission and affects layout-engine width math; capsule + flex are v0.2+ per spec. Separate bead.

Depends on lsm-u8u (config parser) and lsm-7kn (theme system — both shipped).
close_reason: Color policy precedence chain (CLI --no-color/--force-color > NO_COLOR env > FORCE_COLOR env > [layout_options].color > auto) + claude_padding width calc. FORCE_COLOR parses 0/false/off as 'absent' per npm/chalk convention. ColorPolicy, ColorOverride, LayoutOptions marked #[non_exhaustive]; LayoutOptions fields flattened (no redundant Option wrappers). 18 new tests (262 lib + 7 integration). Separator styles filed as lsm-1my (powerline needs Nerd Font emission; out of scope here).

title: Publish config.schema.json via schemars + CI drift check
description:
Derive a JSON Schema from the config.toml Rust types using schemars; commit config.schema.json at the repo root and embed via include_str! for offline editor integrations. CI fails when the committed schema is stale relative to the types (regenerate-and-diff check).

Editor integrations (taplo, VS Code, Zed) pick up the schema via the '$schema' key in the user's config, written by 'linesmith init' and 'linesmith presets apply'.

Depends on lsm-u8u (for the Config types to derive from). Dep: schemars.

title: linesmith init + embedded presets (list/apply)
description:
Build the 'onboarding' UX for config: 'linesmith init' prompts via dialoguer (preset/theme/tool), writes config.toml to the XDG path, emits the Claude Code settings.json snippet. 'linesmith presets list' prints available preset names; 'linesmith presets apply <name>' writes a preset's body to the resolved config path (backup existing as config.toml.bak, --force skips confirmation).

Ship 5 embedded presets per docs/ideas/0001-feature-parity-matrix.md and docs/specs/config.md:
- minimal: model + context
- developer: model + workspace + git + context + cost + rate limits
- power-user: everything v0.1, multi-line
- cost-focused: model + context + cost + rate limits (5h+7d)
- worktree-heavy: model + workspace (worktree-styled) + git + context

Depends on lsm-u8u (config core) for the parser + segment registry. Dep: dialoguer.

title: Truncate highest-priority segment before dropping under width pressure
description:
From slice-4 Codex review: the layout engine drops segments whole once total_width exceeds terminal_width, even when a single over-wide segment (e.g. a long workspace name) could be truncated to fit. Result: `linesmith/very-long-feature-branch-name` on a 30-40 col terminal disappears rather than showing a truncated location.

Current design: width.max is an absolute cap applied in collect_items, unconditional on terminal width. That helps when a segment is pathologically wide but doesn't address "terminal is narrower than natural segment width."

Proposed: before dropping the currently-selected-to-drop segment, attempt to truncate it to (segment_width - (total_width - terminal_width)) cells. Only drop when truncation fails (e.g. resulting width below width.min, or segment has no truncatable text).

Requires spec update to docs/specs/segment-system.md §Layout algorithm. Likely needs a per-segment "truncatable: bool" or "min_useful_width" hint so segments like model/cost that shouldn't truncate opt out.

Once this lands, revisit whether built-in segments (workspace especially) should declare width.max at all — they may not need to.

title: Consider Segment::render -> Result<Option<RenderedSegment>, SegmentError>
description: From slice-4 type-design review: current Segment::render returns Option<RenderedSegment> where None means 'hide.' A plugin that fails to render (rhai error, missing field, arithmetic overflow) has no distinct signal — it vanishes indistinguishably from intentional hiding. Evaluate changing the trait to return Result so runtime errors propagate separately. This is a breaking change the moment a real plugin implements the trait, so decide before the plugin slice ships.
close_reason: Shipped in b36a638: Segment::render returns RenderResult = Result<Option<RenderedSegment>, SegmentError>; errors log to stderr and hide. 135 tests green.

title: Lock down RenderedSegment and SegmentDefaults public fields before plugin API
description: From slice-4 type-design review: RenderedSegment has pub text/width/right_separator; the invariant width == text_width(text) is load-bearing but only enforced at construction. Mutating .text silently desyncs width. Same concern on SegmentDefaults's pub fields — currently no builder beyond with_priority so plugin authors needing to set width/default_separator must use struct literal, blocked by #[non_exhaustive]. Options: make fields pub(crate) + add accessors, or add with_width/with_default_separator chainable builders. Decide before plugin runtime ships.
close_reason: Shipped in 3388b2a: RenderedSegment fields pub(crate) with getters, SegmentDefaults gains with_width/with_default_separator chainable builders.

title: Strip control characters from segment output to prevent terminal injection
description: From slice-4 silent-failure review: segment text can contain control chars (ESC, bell, etc.) which `UnicodeWidthChar::width` reports as 0 cells but are pushed into output verbatim. A malicious project dir at `~/work/evil\x1b[2J/` could blank the user terminal on every statusline render. Strip or escape control characters in RenderedSegment::new and/or text_width.
close_reason: Strip char::is_control() chars in RenderedSegment::new and with_separator. Fast no-alloc path when text is clean. Integration-level tests lock hostile project_dir and worktree name cases against regression.

title: Slice 5: File-based cache layer
description: Implement cache layer per docs/specs/segment-system.md. CachePolicy enum: AlwaysFresh, Ttl(Duration), Invalidated{any_of: Vec<CacheInvalidator>, ttl: Option<Duration>}. CacheInvalidator variants: FileChanged(PathBuf) via mtime, ContextFieldChanged(&'static str) via hash, SessionChanged. Storage: one file per segment under XDG_CACHE_HOME/linesmith/ with atomic temp-rename writes. Unlocks rate-limit scraping without blowing the <20ms budget.

title: Slice 3b: Tool detection heuristic + per-tool normalizer split
description: Split the inline claude module in input.rs into crates/linesmith/src/input/normalizers/{mod.rs,claude.rs,qwen.rs,other.rs}. Implement heuristic detection per input-schema.md (QwenCode if 'version' field present; ClaudeCode if 'cost.total_api_duration_ms' present; default ClaudeCode). Also lands the path_tail two-arg refactor from lsm-coc since the split multiplies the footgun.

Implement cost segment rendering '$X.XX' using host-side format_cost_usd helper (per plugin-api.md contract). Claude normalizer maps 'cost' JSON object.

Claude Code doesn't emit this live today (per docs/research/user-demand.md ccstatusline#239) so the segment will be hidden in practice until Claude Code ships the re-emit; document this explicitly in the segment's doc comment.

title: Add docs/research/README.md index

description: Currently bd init created both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with duplicate content. Goal: one source of truth with @import. Approach to evaluate: make AGENTS.md the source of truth (tool-agnostic convention) and have CLAUDE.md just @import it. If bd ever re-injects, run 'bd init --agents-file AGENTS.md' to redirect.

title: Wrap external-crate error types leaking through linesmith's public API
description:
Several external-crate error types leak through public surfaces, coupling our API to third-party crate choices:

1. `cli::parse()` returns `Result<Action, lexopt::Error>` — `lexopt::Error` is public in our API. Swapping lexopt for another arg parser would be a breaking change.
2. `config::ConfigError::Parse { source: toml::de::Error }` — toml's error type is a public field. Swapping the toml crate would break downstream matchers.
3. `input::parse()` probably surfaces `serde_json::Error` somewhere — verify during implementation.

Fix: introduce our own error types that wrap the external ones with `std::error::Error::source()` chains. Pattern:

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ArgParseError(Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>);
impl From<lexopt::Error> for ArgParseError { ... }
impl std::error::Error for ArgParseError { ... }
```

Audit all `pub fn` / `pub struct field` / `pub enum variant` signatures under `crates/linesmith/src/` for external-crate types. Wrap the ones that surface. Domain-legitimate types (`chrono::DateTime<Utc>`, `std::path::PathBuf`, `std::io::Error`) stay as-is.

Motivation: the project values swap-ability for dependency choices. Wrappers make that possible without breaking downstream consumers.

Scope: single focused refactor, no behavior changes. Tests that match on `lexopt::Error` / `toml::de::Error` variants adapt to the new wrapper types.

title: Replace Style.role + Style.fg precedence with Tint enum
description: Follow-up to lsm-7kn (type-design-analyzer). Style currently has both Option<Role> and Option<Color>; precedence 'fg wins over role' is enforced only in resolve_fg(). A Tint::{Role(Role), Fg(Color), None} variant would make the invariant structural (exactly one tint source at compile time) instead of a runtime resolution step.\n\nDecorations stay as bools since they're orthogonal. Public API change, pre-1.0 fine. Pair with the Palette256 newtype refactor for a coherent type-design slice.

title: Make Color::Palette256 disjoint from Palette16 via newtype
description:
Follow-up to lsm-7kn (type-design-analyzer). Color::Palette256(u8) admits n in 0..=15 which overlaps semantically with Palette16(AnsiColor). Two distinct values mean the same color; palette256_to_ansi16 and downgrade have to special-case n<16.

Fix: introduce a newtype Palette256Index(u8) with TryFrom<u8> rejecting n<16, OR redefine Palette256 to only represent 16..=255. Disjoint variants make the taxonomy structural and eliminate the double-path in downgrade.

Breaking change for Color's public API but we're pre-1.0. Do this alongside the Tint refactor (separate bead) for a clean type-design slice.

title: Improve rgb_to_ansi16 + palette256_to_ansi16 accuracy for Catppuccin
description:
Follow-up to lsm-7kn (code-reviewer P90 + P88 findings). Current downgrade heuristics aren't exercised by MVP built-ins (default uses Palette16 directly, minimal is NoColor) but will matter when Catppuccin lands (lsm-b7u) — those are TrueColor themes and users on legacy terminals need reasonable fallbacks.

Two fixes:
1. rgb_to_ansi16: dominance table steals green hues. Example: (130, 220, 30) routes to Yellow via the (_, dominant_g, _, r_hi, _, _) arm even though the color is lime green. Likely need a proper HSV-nearest or weighted nearest-RGB algorithm, or a precomputed lookup against AnsiColor RGB triples.
2. palette256_to_ansi16 grayscale ramp: 0..=7→Black, 8..=15→BrightBlack, 16..=19→White, 20..=23→BrightWhite has a step 15→16 where a 10-point RGB jump flips dark→white. Rebalance the boundaries.

Tests should snapshot Catppuccin mocha/latte under Palette16 and assert plausible output. Filed P3 (not blocking MVP; matters once lsm-b7u is in progress).

title: Extract shared TempDir test helper (dedupe config.rs + lib.rs)
description: Follow-up from lsm-lyf pr-test-analyzer (severity 5). Two byte-identical TempDir structs and tempdir() helpers exist: config.rs::tests (lines ~357-381) and lib.rs::cli_main_tests (bottom of module). Extract to a #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod testutil in lib.rs or src/testutil.rs so future test modules reuse the same helper.\n\nNote: the hand-rolled version skips cleanup on panic (unwind bypasses Drop on some configs). Either document the limitation or adopt the tempfile dev-dep.

title: Surface VarError::NotUnicode in CliEnv::from_process
description:
Follow-up from lsm-lyf code review (silent-failure-hunter, MEDIUM). CliEnv::from_process uses std::env::var(...).ok() which collapses NotUnicode into None. A HOME with invalid UTF-8 becomes indistinguishable from unset, producing a misleading 'HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME both unset' diagnostic from --check-config.

Fix: match on VarError, log NotUnicode to stderr before treating as None. Or switch to env::var_os and lossy-decode with a warning. Path env vars especially deserve this — it's the exact scenario users will hit and struggle to debug.

Pre-existing behavior (detect_config_path had the same drop). Not a regression from lsm-lyf.

title: Propagate stderr through run_with_segments_and_width
description: Follow-up to lsm-lyf. run_with_segments_and_width currently writes its parse-error line directly to io::stderr().lock() (lib.rs:67). That bypasses the stderr sink that cli_main threads through, so cli_main_tests can't capture 'linesmith: parse: ...' messages on malformed JSON — only the '?' stdout marker.\n\nAdd a stderr Write param to run_with_segments_and_width (and plumb through run_with_width / run), or inject a closure. Update integration tests and cli_main_tests to assert stderr content on malformed payloads. Minor touch — mostly signature plumbing.
close_reason: Superseded: addressed in lsm-lyf. Added run_with_segments_width_and_stderr + layout::render_with_warn; cli_main routes all render-path diagnostics through the injected stderr sink.

title: Harden segment text against Unicode spoofing (bidi overrides, zero-width chars)
description: Follow-up to lsm-8y0. The char::is_control() sanitizer strips C0/C1/DEL but permits Unicode bidi-override and zero-width chars that enable visual spoofing without emitting escape sequences: U+202E RLO, U+200E/U+200F LRM/RLM, U+2066–U+2069 LRI/RLI/FSI/PDI, U+200B/U+200C/U+200D ZWSP/ZWNJ/ZWJ. A project dir named 'linesmith\u{202E}exe.txt' could render deceptively (Trojan Source, CVE-2021-42574). Out of lsm-8y0 scope (which targeted terminal injection, not visual spoofing). Decide: strip category Cf + selected bidi overrides, or normalize via unicode-security crate. Add tests covering RLO/ZWJ/ZWSP in worktree names and project_dir basenames.

title: Add test covering Config::from_str via .parse::<Config>() turbofish
description:
From lsm-u8u test-coverage review: Config implements FromStr, but every test call uses Config::from_str(...) directly. Nothing exercises s.parse::<Config>() or let c: Config = s.parse()? — the documented idiomatic Rust shape.

Low-severity but trivial: one test anywhere that does 'toml-string'.parse::<Config>()? (or let c: Config = s.parse()?) would pin the ergonomic against a future FromStr refactor that accidentally breaks trait-method dispatch.

title: Revisit build_segments warn callback API shape before 1.0
description:
From lsm-u8u final code review: build_segments takes impl FnMut(&str) which is ergonomic but has two post-1.0 pains:
1. Monomorphizes per caller — binary bloat grows with plugin count.
2. Can't add a second callback or change shape without a breaking change.

Options to evaluate:
A. &mut dyn FnMut(&str) — one codegen, slightly less ergonomic.
B. Return (Vec<Box<dyn Segment>>, Vec<Warning>) — caller chooses sink.
C. Typed Warning enum (already flagged earlier) — works well with option B.

Pick before 1.0 tag so the signature doesn't churn for plugin-era consumers.

title: Honor macOS Application Support path as config fallback
description:
From lsm-u8u Codex review (P1): docs/specs/config.md §File location precedence step 5 says macOS should fall back to '~/Library/Application Support/linesmith/config.toml' when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset, after the ~/.config path.

Current config::resolve_config_path ignores this macOS convention, so a Mac-first user who puts their config in Application Support will have it silently ignored.

Fix: add a platform-conditional fallback after home/.config:

    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    if xdg_config_home is None {
        check ~/Library/Application Support/linesmith/config.toml
    }

Low user impact today (nothing released), but easy to get right before 0.1 tag.

title: Consider builder pattern for linesmith::run* entries before SemVer lock
Distinguish env::VarError::NotUnicode from NotPresent in config path resolution
description:
From slice-8 silent-failure review: config.rs:detect_config_path uses std::env::var(...).ok() which collapses VarError::NotUnicode (non-UTF-8 env value) into the same 'unset' case as NotPresent.

Extremely rare in practice (pathological locales / filesystem paths with invalid UTF-8), but when it hits the user sees 'echo $HOME shows something but linesmith acts like HOME is unset' with no diagnostic.

Fix: match explicitly on VarError, log to stderr on NotUnicode, preserve .ok() fast-path for NotPresent.

title: Surface config parse/load errors visibly in rendered line, not just stderr
description:
From slice-8 (lsm-u8u) silent-failure review: when Config::load fails (parse error, permissions), main.rs logs one line to stderr then silently falls back to built-in defaults. Claude Code may not display stderr at all; user edits their config, saves, sees no change, has no clue why.

Proposal: on config load error in normal run mode, emit a visible sentinel segment at the far left (e.g. '⚠ cfg' with role 'error'). The user sees it immediately, runs 'linesmith --check-config' for details.

Decision needed: does 'never crash the terminal' preclude rendering an error marker, or is a one-cell sentinel acceptable? --check-config already handles the strict path.

Related: review also flagged that the current one-stderr-line-per-invocation is near-silent given the statusline runs once per prompt.

title: Rename Separator::None to avoid Option::None shadowing in match arms
description: From slice-4 type-design review: the Separator variant 'None' shadows Option::None when brought into scope via 'use Separator::*'. Readability footgun. Consider 'Empty' or 'NoSeparator' before plugins depend on the name.

title: Introduce Priority newtype with named constants for SegmentDefaults
description: From slice-4 type-design review: SegmentDefaults.priority is a bare u8, and the 'descending drop order, 0 never drops' semantics are encoded in the layout engine. Plugin authors will stare at raw u8 values. Add either a Priority newtype with Priority::never_drop() / default() / drop_first() constructors, or at minimum pub const NEVER_DROPS/DEFAULT/DROP_FIRST constants on SegmentDefaults for vocabulary.

title: Probe /dev/tty for terminal width before falling back to 200
description: From slice-4 review: when stdout/stderr/stdin are piped (Claude Code statusline case), terminal_size() returns None and we fall through to COLUMNS (rarely exported) then 200. Starship and ccstatusline open /dev/tty directly via ioctl to get real width. Add this as a middle step before the 200 constant fallback.

title: Log to stderr when layout overflows with only priority-0 segments remaining
description: From slice-4 review: when the drop loop exits with total_width still > terminal_width (all remaining are priority-0), the line renders overfull silently. Spec says this is intentional, but users have no hint linesmith made the call. Add debug-gated stderr log naming the overfull-by-N cells count.

title: Emit stderr breadcrumb when text_width saturates at u16::MAX
description: From slice-4 silent-failure review: a segment producing text wider than u16::MAX cells (plugin bug or pathological input) is silently clamped to u16::MAX with no diagnostic. Add a debug-only stderr log when UnicodeWidthStr::width > u16::MAX so misbehaving plugins are discoverable.

title: Slice 3 review follow-ups: cosmetic/stylistic items
description: Non-blocking reviewer suggestions deferred from slice 3. (1) Named ParseEffortLevelError instead of FromStr Err=(); breaking change if EffortLevel becomes public API — revisit. (2) EffortLevel::XHigh → VeryHigh rename; keep 'xhigh' wire slug. (3) RateLimits::windows() tuple accessor returning (Option<&>, Option<&>) for callers wanting both windows at once. (4) format_countdown_until 'expired' variant when resets_at < now (vs current 'now' collapse). (5) Far-future countdown clamp (>999d → e.g. '>2y').

title: Workspace segment: distinguish non-UTF-8 from missing basename
description: WorkspaceSegment currently collapses two silent-None cases: (1) project_dir has no basename (e.g. '/'), (2) project_dir basename is not valid UTF-8. Slice-1 reviewer flagged this as a debug-visibility gap. When structured logging lands (part of the rendering pipeline work), distinguish the cases: no-basename is a legitimate render-None; non-UTF-8 should emit a one-shot debug log to stderr so the user can diagnose. No action today — requires logging infrastructure that arrives with slice-5 cache + slice-8 config work.

title: Slice 2 review follow-up: refactor path_tail to two-arg helpers
description: Reviewers flagged path_tail as fragile — silently fails if a JSON key contains a literal dot. Current keys are safe. Fix when the second tool normalizer is added (input/normalizers/*.rs split), since each new normalizer multiplies the footgun. Alternative: two-arg helpers (key: &str for lookup, path: &str for error reporting).

title: Integrate beads hooks into lefthook
description: Wire beads' git hooks through lefthook.yml rather than via bd's own core.hooksPath installation. Target hooks: prepare-commit-msg (agent identity trailer for forensics), post-merge (auto-import issues after pull/merge), post-checkout (sync on branch switch), pre-push (validation before push). Each is a ~3-line lefthook entry that runs 'bd hooks run <event>'. Defer until we have a git remote or start using branches — most of these are no-ops in current solo/local setup. Reference: bd hooks --help for event semantics.
close_reason: Beads hooks integrated via lefthook for all 5 events (pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg, post-merge, post-checkout, pre-push). Extracted safety shim into .lefthook/bd-hook.sh (exit 3/124 swallow, optional timeout via coreutils, graceful no-op on macOS). Verified end-to-end: commit e7f3b06 fired hooks, bd exported 8 issues and 3 memories during pre-commit. Research sources: jdelfino/eval lefthook.yml, beads v0.61 shim .beads/hooks/*.

value: User demand research for Claude Code statuslines (ranked by signal strength): (1) Rate-limit/plan-usage visibility — 44+ reactions on anthropics/claude-code#8412, loudest single signal. Scrape from API headers like ccusage does. (2) Effort/thinking level visibility — 13+ separate issues, CC doesn't re-emit on /effort change. (3) Accurate context % — breaks in 1M context, post-/compact, post-/resume, during 429s. Table stakes, nobody has nailed it. (4) Worktree isolation — model/state leaks across worktrees, ccstatusline#190. (5) Preset onboarding — ccstatusline#42/#226/#277. (6) Burn-rate + survival projection — AndrewTKent mockup #43271. (7) Live skill/agent/MCP visibility — claude-hud at 19.8k stars proves demand. (8) Cache-hit/cache-creation countdown. Top complaints: npx spawns 30+ processes/3GB RAM (ccstatusline#103, #22, chongdashu PR#4), supply-chain risk of @latest (#298), context % wrong more often than right, rendering brittle across tmux/iTerm/IntelliJ/Windows. Competitors: ccstatusline (7.7k TS dominant), CCometixLine (2.7k Rust/TOML), claude-powerline/Owloops (1k TS), claude-hud (19.8k plugin-style), claudia-statusline (Rust+SQLite), felipeelias (Go/TOML). No tool has real plugin API — biggest architectural gap.

Claude Code statusline API contract: spawned per prompt with 300ms debounce, rich JSON on stdin with model {id, display_name}, cwd, workspace {current_dir, project_dir, added_dirs, git_worktree {name, path}}, context_window {used_percentage, context_window_size, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, current_usage {input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens}}, cost {total_cost_usd, total_duration_ms, total_api_duration_ms, total_lines_added, total_lines_removed}, rate_limits {five_hour, seven_day — Pro/Max only}, output_style, vim, agent. Plain text stdout, ANSI + OSC 8 hyperlinks, multi-line OK, no timeout. current_usage null before first API call. Docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline

linesmith project vision: new AI coding CLI status line tool in Rust (tool-agnostic — supports Claude Code + Qwen Code today, Codex/Copilot when they ship their statusLine APIs). Differentiators: (1) real plugin API via rhai scripting — none exist in ecosystem, all tools hardcode widgets; (2) correctness-first on context %/rate limits/worktree isolation — biggest user pains per research; (3) curated presets for onboarding (Catppuccin/Dracula/Nord/Gruvbox/Tokyo Night/Rose Pine + minimal/default); (4) single-binary (~3-5MB) kills npx supply-chain risk. Architecture: segment/widget system with priority/width hints, file-based caching, async, conditional visibility, sub-composition. GitHub: oakoss/linesmith. Stack: Rust + serde_json + owo-colors + gix + toml + rhai + ureq + lexopt + dialoguer + terminal_size + supports-hyperlinks + cargo-dist.
